protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; performs the file-08 property-pin rewrite D-033 authorized under MF-6
summary: I reproduced all fifteen segment hashes independently and every one matches, plus the §7.10 pin the extraction rule cites as its worked example. More importantly I did not stop at the convenience line ranges, because the draft itself says the delimiters are the pin: I confirmed every start line is the named delimiter and every end boundary is correct under the stated rule, including the case where the freeze numbers §7.8 before §7.7 and the positional rule handles it correctly. The correspondence between pins and cited properties is exact in both directions -- fifteen pins against the fifteen properties the five row cells name, nothing pinned that is not cited and nothing cited left unpinned. D-033 is characterized correctly as authorizing and expressly not performing. Every whole-file digest matches live bytes, both retired scope sentences genuinely exist in DR-001's cell, '0/11 SATISFIED' is accurate, and no register, freeze, blueprint or claim-matrix file is touched in this cycle. One SHOULD-FIX blocks CONSENT: file 08's own pin-accounting note counts six freeze pins -- five in this register plus one in the claim matrix -- and this entry converts five and says nothing about the sixth, while it does expressly name the two other conversions it declines.

objections.location: Property-pins table and the paragraph beginning 'DR-001's source-pin cell already names the three manifests'
objections.claim: The register tracks six whole-document freeze pins as one set. This entry converts the five in file 08 and is silent on the sixth, in the claim matrix, even though the entry's own practice elsewhere is to name what it declines to convert and why.
evidence: File 08's 'Pin re-move — 2026-08-13 (D-014)' note states the set explicitly: 'six freeze pins — five in this register (DR-004, DR-005, DR-006, DR-011, DR-012) plus one in the claim matrix (**Key sealed laws**)'.

I measured the whole-file freeze digest e809d439… in file 08 and found 6 occurrences: five row cells at lines 37, 38, 39, 44, 45 and one inside that accounting note at line 262. The blueprint digest 909394c5… occurs twice: DR-011's cell at line 44 and the same note.

The sixth pin is docs/v2/architecture/09-v1-to-v2-claim-matrix.md line 54: '| Key sealed laws | `IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md` `e809d439…` | §6 laws **1–19 in full**, …'. It is a whole-document freeze digest carried as a standing citation.

D-044 accounts for its other two declined conversions by name: 'DR-001's source-pin cell already names the three manifests, not a freeze whole-file digest. Those three remain cited. This entry does not convert them.' and 'R2-FINAL-03 stays the named residual already routed at DR-011-R10; it is not given a new section pin here.' The claim-matrix pin gets neither treatment.
objections.iAmNotAskingForTheConversion: I accept that converting it here would likely be wrong. D-044's subject line scopes to 'file 08 citation form and DR-001 live scope clause only', the claim matrix is file 09, and D-033 clause 1 reaches 'DR-001 (and … DR-004 / DR-005 / DR-006 / DR-011 / DR-012) standing citations' rather than another document's own rows. Converting a file-09 citation would be a separate register-content act needing its own D-000 commit, exactly as D-033 required for file 08. The ask is to name it and route it, not to fold it in.
objections.whyItMatters: The consequence is concrete rather than editorial. After this entry lands, five of the six tracked pins stop re-opening their rows on freeze motion that does not touch a cited property, and one does not. That sixth citation remains on the treadmill D-033 exists to end, and nothing in the register says so or names who closes it. A reader reconciling D-044 against file 08's own six-pin accounting finds five converted and one unexplained, which is exactly the ambiguity the other two named exclusions exist to prevent.
objections.remedy: Add one sentence in the form the entry already uses: name the claim-matrix 'Key sealed laws' pin, state that it is outside this entry's file-08 scope and outside D-033 clause 1's DR-row scope, and say whether it is routed to a later act or deliberately left whole-document.

notesRecorded.observation: The sentence 'A baseline refresh re-opens it' occurs TWICE inside DR-001's row, not once. I measured occurrences within line 34 itself: 'A baseline refresh re-opens it' twice, 'any pinned-source motion re-opens the row' once.
notesRecorded.whyItIsOnlyANote: Clause 2's wording is already sufficient -- it says 'The sentences … cease to be live scope', which covers both instances, and both instances sit inside DR-001's row, which is precisely what clause 2 scopes to. There is no defect in the entry's text.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecordingAtAll: This entry authorizes a byte-level rewrite of that cell, and a performing commit that retires one occurrence and misses the duplicate would leave DR-001 still re-opening on baseline refresh -- defeating the entire purpose while appearing to have executed clause 2. The duplicate is not visible without measuring inside the row, since the whole row is a single line. Recording it so the executor and the turn-2 reviewer can check for two removals rather than one.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 6eb6f8692aa9225155c5877d34864968d32f814d469c79ec4142774d679c9865 both times, matching the dispatch's expected digest. No drift.

The attack 'unreproducible segment hash' fails on all fifteen. I extracted each range myself with sed and hashed it: DR-004 freeze §3.1 580-603 19c6a3eb…; DR-005 EVIDENCE 388 fe85576b…, TM 391 dcbfb191…, OPERABILITY 383 dc1f8ef8…; DR-006 FACT-PLANE 379 d5891fa5…, §7.1 1675-2267 30a2ff0a…, §9 4674-5287 01e36920…, §6 law 6 1442-1463 0e3d3c69…, §6 law 19 1531-1580 671e2247…; DR-011 blueprint §1.1 121-836 39843bda…, freeze §3 ledger 285-691 9bb9765b…, §7 1581-4609 9eeb80c0…, §7.8 3884-4174 f305c688…, §7.9 4311-4448 a8db5cc1…; DR-012 §6 law 17 1497-1498 cb2331f2…. Every one reproduces exactly.

The §7.10 pin the extraction rule offers as its worked example also reproduces: lines 4449-4609 give 7bfa72c40b08381ceb0e9a815f6e0746f7c9c47f14b6b08496ef03980495c1ca, the value the draft states. The draft additionally names the wrong reading 32da6d14… so a re-deriver can tell which reading produced which hash, which is the right disclosure to carry.

I did not stop at the line ranges, because the draft states 'Line ranges below are convenience … The delimiters are the pin.' I verified every start line IS the named delimiter: line 580 is '### 3.1 Phase-1A insertion — mandatory', 1675 is '### 7.1 Parked identity recipes…', 4674 is '## 9. Phase-4 verification record', 1442 begins '6. `RequestId`', 1531 begins '19. **An identity namespace', 121 is '### 1.1 Normative byte set…', 285 is '## 3. Surface disposition ledger', 1581 is '## 7. Named non-blocking residuals and parks', 3884 is '### 7.8 Companion instruments…', 4311 is '### 7.9 Structural: applying a successor…', 1497 begins '17. `implementable: true`', and the four table rows begin '| EVIDENCE |', '| TM |', '| OPERABILITY |', '| FACT-PLANE / C-1 |'. Fifteen for fifteen.

I verified every END boundary against the stated rule rather than trusting the range. Each range's next line is the correct terminator: §3.1 ends before '### 3.2', §7.1 before '### 7.2', §9 before '## 10.', law 6 before '7. Product admission…', law 19 before '## 7.', blueprint §1.1 before '## 2.', §3 ledger before '## 4.', §7 before '## 8.', §7.9 before '### 7.10', law 17 before '18. **Closed-scalar admission…'. Section ranges correctly swallow their own subheadings, which is what 'same or higher level' requires.

One end boundary deserves explicit record because it looks wrong and is right. §7.8 spans 3884-4174 and the next heading is '### 7.7 Editing hazard…' -- the freeze numbers §7.8 ahead of §7.7 in document order. The extraction rule is positional ('next heading of the same or higher level'), not numeric, so it handles the freeze's own disorder correctly and the hash reproduces. A rule keyed to section numbers would have produced a different segment here.

The attack 'pins a section the named cell does not cite' fails, and the correspondence is exact in both directions. DR-004's cell cites '§3.1; product CD-RT-5.whatThisDecisionDoesNOTDo' and gets one §3.1 pin with the selector expressly retained. DR-005's cites '§3 EVIDENCE/TM/OPERABILITY; operability.v10' and gets those three row pins with the v10 G19 instrument pin expressly retained. DR-006's cites '§3 FACT-PLANE, §7.1/§9, laws 6/19' and gets exactly those five. DR-011's cites '§1.1; freeze …' and '§3/§7/§7.8/§7.9 and R2-FINAL-03' and gets those five with R2-FINAL-03 expressly addressed. DR-012's cites '§6 law 17' and gets that one. Nothing is pinned that is not cited; nothing cited is left unpinned.

The attack 'D-033 cited as performing the rewrite' fails. Every reference is correct: the decision-type line says D-033 'authorized and refused to perform in the same commit (D-001 MF-6)', and the measured-inputs row says 'clause 2 authorizes this rewrite and does not perform it'. I read adopted D-033 and its clause 2 says exactly that: 'This entry authorizes that rewrite. It does not perform it. Performing it is a file-08 content change and needs its own D-000-reviewed commit (D-001 MF-6).' The clause-1 and clause-4 citations are also accurate.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all four whole-file pins: freeze e809d439…, blueprint 909394c5… (which I located by digest sweep at docs/coop/IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md rather than assuming a path), COORD 726b472e…, file 08 877e36d3…. The two adoption commits are also correct: D-033 at ac48808 and D-043 at a5d3719, both confirmed in git log.

The attack 'scope rewrite that still re-opens on any baseline or freeze motion' fails. Clause 2's replacement clause re-opens only on a cited-property change -- path missing, named section/selector/law/row unresolvable, or segment hash mismatch -- and expressly states that whole-document motion of the freeze, blueprint, baseline or register that does not change a cited property does not re-open the row. That is the treadmill's actual mechanism, closed at the right place.

The two sentences clause 2 retires are real, not phantom text. Both appear in file 08 at line 34, DR-001's row: 'A baseline refresh re-opens it' and 'any pinned-source motion re-opens the row'. Both are inside the row clause 2 scopes to. The duplicate occurrence of the first is the note above.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or SATISFIED re-record' fails. All eight occurrences are negative or historical: the subject line's 'Not SATISFIED re-record', clause 3's 'The 2026-08-13 SATISFIED disposition stays history' and 'This entry is not that re-record', clause 6's 'No row becomes SATISFIED', the rejected alternative, and the readiness effect's 'Zero SATISFIED'. Preserving the 2026-08-13 disposition as history rather than deleting it is the correct handling.

'Condition 1 still 0/11 SATISFIED' is accurate, checked row by row. DR-001 is OPEN, DR-002 through DR-007 and DR-009 through DR-011 are HARD-BLOCKED, and DR-008 is PARTIALLY SATISFIED -- which is not SATISFIED. No row of the eleven is SATISFIED.

The attack 'MEASURED regeneration of baseline/status manifests in this act' fails. Clause 4 states the entry does not edit v1-authority-baseline.json or v1-status-evidence.json, that they stay whole-document until a later MEASURED regeneration, and that this entry is not that regeneration. The rejected alternative repeats it citing D-001 C3 / MF-8.

The attacks 'DESIGN-READY / new file-08 status token', 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation authorization', and 'freeze / blueprint motion' all fail. Clause 5 keeps the status vocabulary closed citing D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03; clause 6 states condition 5 unchanged, no freeze motion, no blueprint, no docs/v2/implementation/; DESIGN-READY is rejected in the alternatives citing D-033 clause 4, which does forbid a new status token.

File 08, the freeze, the blueprint, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md and the claim matrix are all unmodified in git, so nothing has been pre-applied ahead of this entry's own adoption, consistent with the dispatch's statement that file 08 is not edited in this review cycle.

Clause 7's snapshot update is correctly bounded: it updates the dated current-position block's condition-1 clause so its leading label still matches the DR-001 cell, and states 'Rows remain authoritative.' It does not make the snapshot a second source of truth.

The reversibility statement is honest about becoming compound: 'Compound after the rewrite lands: overturn requires reverting or superseding this commit (C-D044) and restoring the prior scope clause.' That matches adopted D-033's own reversibility note and does not overstate how cheaply this can be undone.

Examined and declined: clause 3 restates D-033 clause 3's SATISFIED gate as 'SATISFIED only after independent review', where D-033 says 'SATISFIED only after DR-204 audits the disposition' -- a less specific referent, and DR-204 is named zero times in this draft. I decline to grade it because the operative constraint survives, clause 3 points at D-001 as the governing authority for the two-stage act rather than redefining it, and D-001's own text supplies the general framing ('SATISFIED requires independent review') alongside the DR-204 one. I record it because this is the single place where the entry's restatement is looser than its source, and the entry's subject is citation precision.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of D-044. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

Whether the freeze and blueprint whole-file digests are themselves the right heads. I verified the cited digests match the live files; I did not audit whether a successor freeze or blueprint exists that should be the pinned head instead.

The substantive content of the fifteen pinned sections. I verified each segment's boundaries and hash and that each is cited by its row, not that the pinned text actually discharges what the row needs from it. That is the row owners' question, and it is the same limit I have carried on every property-pin review in this series.

The claim-matrix pin's own correctness beyond its existence and form. I measured that it is a whole-document freeze digest at file 09 line 54 carrying '§6 laws 1–19 in full'; I did not compute a segment hash for §6 or judge whether it should be converted, only that this entry neither converts nor names it.

Whether any whole-document pin exists in a file I did not sweep. I enumerated freeze and blueprint whole-file digests in file 08 and in the claim matrix, the two the register's own accounting note identifies. I did not sweep every document in the repository for standing citations that D-033 clause 1 might reach.

Line-range stability under any future freeze motion. The draft is explicit that ranges are convenience and delimiters are the pin, which is the correct design; I verified both agree today and did not model what happens to the convenience column after the next freeze move.

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one SHOULD-FIX, and I want the shape of that on the record because this is the most carefully built draft in the series so far. Fifteen segment hashes reproduce, the delimiter rule holds at both ends of every segment including the one place the freeze's own section numbering runs backwards, the pin set matches the cited-property set exactly in both directions, and every characterization of D-033 is faithful to its adopted bytes. My objection is a silence, not an error: file 08's own accounting names six freeze pins, this entry converts five, and the sixth is neither converted nor named -- while the entry twice demonstrates that naming a declined conversion is its practice. One sentence closes it.
